_comment: Scenario-staged rout-then-ANNIHILATION demo: a lone low-morale (1) player infantry block of 12 is charged head-on by two 12-horse cavalry troops and BREAKS -- it enters routing (drawn faded) and flees. The squadrons are shallow and spawn close so their facing-front is in spatha reach at regiment contact. Routing units are still valid combat targets, and the cavalry (8.5 m/s sprint) are faster than the fleeing infantry (4.0 m/s sprint, 1.3 x that in flight), so pursuit is relentless: each routed man runs on his own from the riders he sees toward his own back edge (SoldierFlightStep), the runners scatter, and each rider rides at the runner nearest him and cuts him down on the move (SoldierPursuitStep; at Cannae the Numidian horse pursued the fleeing Roman cavalry and cut most of them down, Polybius 3.116). The casualties keep its morale from recovering, so it never rallies and is ANNIHILATED (soldiers reach zero) rather than escaping or rallying. The scene runs on a custom tall map (field 1600x2400, flat) with every actor staged in the deep south, so the flight has room; a second, safe player unit (140 Spearmen) stays in the fight so the battle doesn't declare defeat the instant the infantry routs. Measured with dense 2-tick FULL dumps on seeds 0 to 4, 2026-11-13 on #1949's branch: it routs by tick 100 and is still routing at tick 300 (pinned) with 4 to 8 of its 12 men left; the lead squadron (uid 3) is after it (target_enemy_uid 0) inside ticks 200 to 300 on every seed (pinned); and the last runner falls at tick 616 on the clip's own seed (seed 0), 520 on seed 1, 530 on seed 3, 492 on seed 4, and at about tick 1150 on seed 2, where a straggler who ran off from the rest is ridden down last (absent inside ticks 300 to 1200, pinned). On main c36560fa it was caught at tick 420, fought on the move to tick 542 and cut down between ticks 648 and 650. The pins were: ROUTING at tick 540, uid 3 targeting it and engaged in melee inside ticks 480 to 600, and gone inside ticks 610 to 700. The bottom-up flight and the riders' own pursuit (#1949) run it down earlier on four seeds and later on one, so the windows move to cover every seed, and the engaged pin is retired: riders who cut runners down on the move are not a block engaged in melee. Camera frames the clash and then pans with the chase (website/tools/demo-catalog.sh records 360 frames at 30 fps, to tick 720, which shows the kill on every seed but seed 2). No player input needed. (A unit that truly breaks free instead recovers cleanly -- see test/unit/test_morale_recovery_demo_scenario.gd for that case in isolation.)

misslotted.reason: misslotted reads uid3 (the lead cavalry troop) 0.5 against 0.25 on seed 1, and passes on seeds 0, 2, 3 and 4 (dense 2-tick FULL dumps, measured 2026-11-13 on #1949's branch). Analysing the dump cut off at successive ticks, it passes through tick 900 and fails only once the samples reach tick 1200: the troop has then been marching on the Spearmen (target uid 1) since about tick 560, long after it formed up where its riders stood at the end of its chase (re-deal stamped at tick 521, whose transit window closed long before). The reading is that long march, tracked in #1983.

follow_error.reason: follow_error reads uid2 (the trailing cavalry troop) 94.35 against 30 on seed 2, and passes on seeds 0, 1, 3 and 4 (dense 2-tick FULL dumps, measured 2026-11-13 on #1949's branch). Analysing the dump cut off at successive ticks, it passes through tick 1080 and fails only once the samples reach tick 1200: the troop has then been marching on the Spearmen (target uid 1) since tick 542, more than 500 ticks after it formed up where its riders stood at the end of its chase (re-deal stamped at tick 543, whose transit window closed long before). The reading is that long march, tracked in #1983.
